COURT OF INTERNATIONAL TRADE
Court No. 25-00031
SEAFOOD EXPORTERS ASSOCIATION OF INDIA,
Plaintiff,
v.
UNITED STATES,
Defendant,
and
AD HOC SHRIMP TRADE ACTION COMMITTEE
and
AMERICAN SHRIMP PROCESSORS
ASSOCIATIO
items.summary: The U.S. Court of International Trade sustained the International Trade Commission's determination that subsidized shrimp imports from India, Ecuador, and Vietnam caused material injury to the domestic shrimp industry. The court rejected the Indian exporters' argument that frozen cooked shrimp should be classified separately from frozen raw shrimp, affirming the ITC's definition of a single domestic like product encompassing both varieties. The court also rejected the claim that imports fill a supply gap that domestic producers cannot serve.
